epic.title: Garden 2027: design in February, work March to May
epic.description:
Design first: no repair work until the garden is designed, in whatever tool exists then. The design places somewhere to sit and eat, growing things, a shed or workshop for FixForward's bench and storage, and somewhere safe for a child. Then the full May plan, re-dated across Saturdays from March to May 2027, with a budget of about £100 a month. Tools owned: pressure washer with patio head, weed puller, electric mower, seeder, aerator.

## Order
garden.01 (6 February). Then weeds (garden.02, 6 March), hedge (garden.03, 13 March), pressure wash (garden.04, 20 March), joints (garden.05, 27 March), crack and gatepost (garden.06, 3 April), path-to-fence strip and drain and moss (garden.07 and garden.08, 10 April), lawn (garden.09, 17 April, soil temperature permitting), back corner (garden.10, 24 April), fence after the missing panel (garden.11, 1 May), front strip decision (garden.12, 8 May), shed priced (garden.13, 15 May), done check (garden.14, 29 May).

## Done means
The garden matches the design: sitting and eating, growing, a shed or workshop placed and priced, and safe for a child, with the spring list closed by the end of May 2027.

## Flags
- H4: design first and everything in spring collide with the unbuilt editor, one room at a time and the baby dates; Claude flagged it once and the red team prices it. Not reopened.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs (link filled by the integrator).

## Red team
- Finding 33: This epic and the baby share every weekend from March to the birth; the baby wins. The design, the weeds, the lawn, the back corner and the safe strip stay in spring; the rest moved to July and August.

tickets.title: Hedge trim to the boundary; a note to the neighbour or landlord
tickets.description:
## What
From Saturday 13 March 2027: check the hedge for active nests first, find the boundary, deliver a short note to the neighbour or landlord, then trim to the boundary on your side and clear up. Leave any section with an active nest.

## Why
The May plan includes the hedge trim to the boundary and a note to the neighbour or landlord.

## Done looks like
The hedge trimmed to the boundary, the note delivered, any nest left alone.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
garden.01: the design.

## Red team
- Finding 34: Check for active nests first; if any, wait until August. Bird nesting season runs March to August.

intro.answer: Check for nests first, trim to the boundary, and leave a note for the neighbour or landlord.

sources.label: RSPB: nesting birds and the law

steps.title: Look for nests
steps.body_html: Walk the length of the hedge slowly, look in, and watch for birds flying in and out. March is the start of the nesting season.
steps.expect_html: No active nest seen, or one found.

notes.html: It is an offence to damage or destroy a wild bird's nest while it is in use or being built. If you see one, leave that section until the young have gone (often late summer).

steps.title: Find the boundary
steps.body_html: Find the boundary line (fence posts or the deeds plan). You trim back to your side of it.

steps.title: Write the note
steps.body_html: Write a short, friendly note to the neighbour or landlord saying you will trim the hedge to the boundary on a named day, and asking them to tell you if they object.

steps.title: Trim to the boundary
steps.body_html: Trim the face and top on your side, leaving any section with a nest.

steps.title: Clear up
steps.body_html: Rake and bag the cuttings.

tickets.title: Paving joints: test width and depth first (3 mm by 30 mm for polymeric, else brush-in sand)
tickets.description:
## What
From Saturday 27 March 2027, after the pressure wash: measure joint width and depth at five places, then choose a polymeric jointing compound only if the joints meet the product's minimum (commonly 3 mm wide and 25 to 30 mm deep; some products need 5 mm), else kiln-dried brush-in sand. Filling follows on a dry day as the product says.

## Why
The May plan said test first: polymeric compound needs joints at least 3 mm wide and 30 mm deep, otherwise brush-in sand.

## Done looks like
Width, depth, the filler chosen and the quantity recorded; joints filled.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
garden.04: washed joints.

## Cost
The garden budget in May was about £100 a month. Nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 33: Moved past the birth and the quiet fortnight: every spring Saturday was a baby weekend. Phil can pull it forward on the decisions review.

intro.answer: Measure the joints first: at least 3 mm wide and about 30 mm deep suits polymeric compound; otherwise brush-in sand.

sources.label: EASYJoint data sheet (not for joints under 3 mm)
Bostik Wide Jointing Compound (5 mm minimum width, 25 mm depth)
Pavetuf jointing compound, Jewson (3 to 20 mm wide, 20 mm deep minimum)

steps.title: Measure width at five joints
steps.body_html: At five joints spread across the area, measure the narrowest width in millimetres.

steps.title: Probe the depth
steps.body_html: Push a probe down each joint to the bedding and measure the depth.

steps.title: Pick the filler
steps.body_html: If every joint is at least 3 mm wide and at least 25 mm deep (30 mm preferred), a polymeric compound rated for that width suits. Read the bag's data sheet: some need 5 mm. Otherwise use brush-in kiln-dried sand.

steps.title: Note the quantity
steps.body_html: Note the area in square metres and the number of bags the product gives for that joint size.

tickets.title: Back lawn renovation: scarify, aerate, overseed (ryegrass and fescue), top-dress; edge and holes
tickets.description:
## What
From Saturday 17 April 2027, over five sittings: check the soil is warm enough (about 8 to 10 C at 5 cm), mow short, scarify, aerate, overseed with a hard-wearing ryegrass and fescue mix, top-dress, water, then fill holes and recut the edges. April is the usual spring window; the soil thermometer decides the seeding day, not the date. Scarifying is not in the owned tool list (pressure washer, weed puller, electric mower, seeder, aerator): a spring-tine rake works, or hire or buy a scarifier.

## Why
The May plan's back lawn renovation: scarify, aerate, overseed with a hard-wearing ryegrass and fescue mix, top-dress.

## Done looks like
Seed germinated across the lawn, holes filled, edges clean.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
garden.02: weeds cleared.

## Cost
Seed and top-dressing, and a scarifier if hired or bought; to be priced. The garden budget in May was about £100 a month. Nothing is bought in this run.

intro.answer: Scarify, aerate, overseed with a hard-wearing ryegrass and fescue mix, top-dress, then mend the edges and holes, once the soil is warm.
time: About 1 hour 15 minutes over five sittings, plus watering

sources.label: Homebuilding: best time to scarify a lawn
RHS: lawns, jobs for October (soil at least 7C for germination)
Last Frost Date UK: average frost dates map

hard_part.why: Seeding into cold soil wastes the seed; the date on this ticket is a target, the thermometer decides.

steps.title: Soil temperature
steps.body_html: Push the thermometer about 5 cm in and read it in the morning on three days. Overseeding waits until it is about 8 to 10 C or more.

notes.html: Seed in cold wet soil can rot. In South Yorkshire this is often mid to late April.

steps.title: Mow short
steps.body_html: Mow lower than usual (not scalping) so the scarifier reaches the thatch.

steps.title: Scarify
steps.body_html: Scarify in one direction, then across. The lawn will look rough; that is right. Do not scarify wet or frosty turf.

steps.title: Rake up
steps.body_html: Rake up and bag the debris.

steps.title: Aerate
steps.body_html: Aerate the whole lawn, more on worn or compacted patches, with the soil slightly moist.

steps.title: Overseed
steps.body_html: Set the seeder to the overseeding rate on the seed box and sow in two passes at right angles.

steps.title: Top-dress
steps.body_html: Spread a thin layer of top-dressing and brush it into the holes. The grass should still show through.

steps.title: Water
steps.body_html: Water gently. Keep the seed bed moist until it germinates (often 7 to 14 days).

steps.title: Fill holes
steps.body_html: Fill holes with soil, firm, and seed.

steps.title: Cut the edges
steps.body_html: Recut the lawn edge to a clean line.
